Aṃśatrayīvicāra
mīm. MD. 4397. conjectural title of a fr. of a C. on the Bhāṭṭadīpikā beginning near I. ii. 1; not Śambhubhaṭṭa's Prabhāvalī, Vāñcheśvara's Bhāṭṭacintāmaṇi, or Bhāskararāya's Bhāṭṭacandrikā (-candrodaya).

Aṃśadaśā
jy. Rice 28. C.. Aṁśakadaśā, Whish p. 286.

Aṃśanāḍīphala(keralīya)
jy. Mysore I. p. 342. III. p. 9.

Aṃśaphala
jy. consequences of birth in the 12 Aṁśas of the different Lagnas. MD. 13599. Trav. Uni. 2519J.

Aṃśaphalavicāra
jy. TCD. 627 (mixed with Malayalam). Trav. Uni. T. M. 119.

Aṃśabali
jy.-dh. propitiatory rites for averting the evils concomitant with an. Aṁśa of a man's Rāśi. MD. 3228.

Aṃśalagnadaśābhuktinirūpaṇa
jy. on finding out the Lagna an. the planetary periods an. sub-periods. MD. 13600.

Aṃśaviveka
Q. in the Bhāgavatatātparya of Madhvācārya. BNK. Sarma, His.. of Dvai. Lit. I. App. I. p. 354.

Aṃśaśivarahasya
Śaiva rel. R. A. Sastri II. p. 172 (Ms. in Madura).

Aṃśāvataraṇa
by Vyāsa. NP. IV. 8. Ch.. 59-64 of Ādiparvan of the M. Bhā.
--C. by Nīlakaṇṭha. NP. IV. 12. [Page001-b]

Aṃśāvataraṇa
on the partial incarnations of Viṣṇu; also on the origins of the heroes an. demons of mythology; in 95 verses; title in the first verse ‘Aṁśāveśāvatāraṇa’; seems to be ref. to also a. Aṁśāṁśinirṇaya.
by Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍita, son of Trivikrama Paṇḍita.
Baroda 6627 (b). IO. 7047. Mysore I. p. 503 (?) (Aṁśāvatārādinirṇaya).
Pt.. by R. S. Sarma, Kumbhakonam.

āṃśāvataraṇa
6th upaparvan. BORI. 359 of Viś. I. Mysore N. D. VI. 16706 (inc.).

Aṃśumat
Aṁśumat, Aṁśumatkalpa, Aṁśumadbheda, Aṁśumattantra (see below), Aṁśumānakalpa--all these refer to the same text, one of the 28 Śaiva Āgamas (MD. 5420) (IO. 6085, 6113), dealing with, among other things, TempleArchitecture, Iconography an. Consecration.
The Kāśyapamata, Kāśyapaśilpa or the Aṁśumatkāśyapīya (see next entry) represents its Śilpa portion. Ānandāśrama Ed.. No. 95, Kāśyapaśilpa, in 88 chs., is the same. P. K. Acharya, however, wrongly takes each of these a. separate in his Dict. of Hindu Architecture, p.. 750, 756-9.
Aufrecht's Aṁśumadbhedasaṅgraha, Vedānta, ascribed to Kāśyapa, Oppert [Page002-a. I. 5875, is evidently a. epitome of the Aṁśumadbhedāgama.
--Brahmaliṅgapratiṣṭhāvidhi from the Aṁśumat. Adyar II. p. 193a.
